public_rationale: OpenAI's o1 launch post, published on 12 September 2024, compares o1 with GPT-4o. On the 2024 AIME, GPT-4o solved about 12% of problems and o1 about 74% with a single sample, roughly 6x (e1). In the post's Appendix A table (e2), o1 scores 78.0 on GPQA Diamond against GPT-4o's 56.1, about 1.4x. MATH goes from 60.3 to 94.8 and MMLU from 88.0 to 90.8. The largest ratios in that table are about 8x, for AIME pass@1 (9.3 to 74.4) and the CodeForces percentile (11.0 to 89.0). None of the scores in the launch post comes near 100x. Marcus's statement that OpenAI's own data does not show o1 as 100 times better than GPT-4 holds for these published results.
limitations: OpenAI's baseline is GPT-4o, not the original GPT-4.
Only the launch post was checked, not the o1 system card or later OpenAI publications.
'Better' is not defined. Ratios of benchmark scores are one reasonable measure, and scores with a fixed maximum limit how large a ratio can be.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: By OpenAI's own data, o1 is certainly not 100 times better than GPT-4.

statement.document_title: An epidemic of weirdly precise AI butt facts

from_speaker: is OpenAI's o1 100 times better than GPT4?
our_interpretation: Plain reading: none of OpenAI's own published o1 evaluations show anything close to a hundredfold gain over GPT-4-class models.
OpenAI's launch post compares o1 with GPT-4o, its GPT-4-family model at the time. I treat that as the 'GPT4' comparison OpenAI's own data offers.
The period is the state of OpenAI's published o1 data at the post date: from o1's announcement on 2024-09-12 to 2024-10-30.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI's published o1 results show gains well below 100x over GPT-4/GPT-4o on its reported metrics.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An OpenAI-published metric shows o1 roughly 100 times better than GPT-4 or GPT-4o.

evidence.excerpt: GPT‑4o only solved on average 12% (1.8/15) of problems. o1 averaged 74% (11.1/15) with a single sample per problem
evidence.explanation: On AIME, one of OpenAI's best showcases for o1, the gain is about sixfold (74% vs 12%), far below 100x.
On GPQA Diamond, GPT-4o scored 56.1 and o1 78.0, a gain of about 1.4x. Other rows (MMLU 88.0 vs 90.8, MATH 60.3 vs 94.8) also show modest gains.
